question: What is the annual dropout rate of secondary school students in India as per the 2020-21 report by Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.146**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The annual dropout rate of secondary school students in India for the year 2020-21 is **14.6%** as per the UDISE+ report.
 
• The Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+) collects data on multiple parameters such as student enrolment, dropout rates, and school infrastructure.
 
• The dropout rate indicates the percentage of students who leave school before completing their secondary education.
 
• This high dropout rate is a significant concern for policymakers aiming to improve educational outcomes in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+)**

 
 
• UDISE+ is a comprehensive database of schools in India, initiated by the Ministry of Education.
 
• It collects data on various parameters such as student enrolment, teacher numbers, infrastructure details, and academic performance.
 
• Data collected through UDISE+ is used to monitor the implementation of various education policies and schemes.
 
• It helps in identifying gaps in educational resources and infrastructure, enabling targeted interventions.
 
 
 
• **Dropout Rate**
 
 
• The dropout rate is the percentage of students who discontinue their education at a specific level.
 
• It is calculated by comparing the number of students enrolled at the beginning of the academic year with those who remain at the end.
 
• High dropout rates can indicate issues such as poor school infrastructure, lack of quality education, financial constraints, or social factors.
 
• Reducing dropout rates is crucial for achieving universal education and improving the overall literacy rate.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Education in India**
 
 
• Secondary education typically covers students aged 14-18 years, encompassing grades 9-12.
 
• It serves as a bridge between primary education and higher education or vocational training.
 
• Ensuring access to quality secondary education is essential for preparing students for future academic and career opportunities.
 
• The government has various schemes in place to promote secondary education, such as scholarships and mid-day meal programs.
